description:
FILED s543b (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-16) while probing #5082's openers.  PRE-EXISTING (base c5f618f2 = the same).  SILENT WRONG in the safe direction (PCL lives where perl dies).

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 | PCL):
    open my $d, "<", "/etc/passwd" or die; opendir $d, "/tmp" or die "o2"; print "opened\n";
    # perl dies: Cannot open $d as a dirhandle: it is already open as a filehandle at - line 1.
    # PCL: opened
    opendir my $e, "/tmp" or die; open $e, "<", "/etc/passwd" or die "o2"; print "opened\n";
    # perl dies: Cannot open $e as a filehandle: it is already open as a dirhandle at - line 1.
    # PCL: opened
(fatal since perl 5.28; a CLOSED handle of the other kind is fine in both.)

WHERE: the openers' install slot (%p-fh-install-arg -> %p-fh-place-check) does not know WHICH opener it serves; the check needs the opener kind (dir vs file) and the openness of the old value (an open stream / an open P-DIRHANDLE record, task #5082's struct).  Low priority: no ordinary program relies on the death.

=== DONE (s543n, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-24; WIP 8 a1fbbf38) ===
%p-open-kind-check: `opendir` on a handle open as a filehandle (a stream or a socket) and `open` on one open as a
dirhandle die before anything is closed -- "Cannot open NAME as a dirhandle: it is already open as a filehandle" and
its twin, NAME the glob's own (`$d`, `FH`, `GEN0`, `$h{...}`; %p-handle-perl-name).  A closed handle of the other kind,
sysopen / pipe / socket on an open dirhandle, and a reopen of the same kind are fine (probed 5.40.3).
